title: The boot chunk could still lose about 37 KB (a lazy features loader) or 5.6 KB (domMin) of framer-motion, each with a recorded risk
acceptance: Either the loader ships with a modulepreload, a retry and give-up path and entry and exit gates, recorded in a DECISIONS entry naming item 140, or an entry records that the savings are not worth the risks.
note: Measured by the W2-L builder: features={() => import(...)} reads index 597,267 B (36,808 B under the shipped 634,075 B, 84,365 B under base 681,632 B) plus a 38,030 B features chunk, so total bytes rise by about 1,222 B and 36.8 KB leave the boot path. Not shipped, on two risks: the title overlay fades in from opacity 0, so a loader shows a blank title until a second request resolves; and a failed request leaves every panel at opacity 0 for good with nothing thrown. To build it: the one-line swap, a modulepreload in vite.config.js (as preloadGameIcons does), a retry and a give-up path (as dragonLoader.js has), the entry and exit gates (app-motion-provider-gates, lazy-motion-exit-gates) awaiting the load, and a DECISIONS entry that names item 140. Close it by building that, or by a DECISIONS entry that the 36.8 KB is not worth the two risks. From REVIEW:w2l:domin-door: domMin (renderer, animation and exit, no gestures) would take another 5,631 B off the boot chunk (PR #60 round-1 mutant B4: index 628,444 B against 634,075 B), but a future whileHover, whileTap or whileInView would render and do nothing; nothing in src uses a gesture prop today. Do it only with a gate that mounts a gesture prop under the provider and reds when it does nothing.

title: domMin in MotionProvider would take another 5,631 B off the boot chunk, and a gesture prop (whileHover, whileTap, whileInView) would then silently do nothing

The real code passed both probes, and the identity mutant stayed green. Fix: stand at the lair for at least three retry cycles, and add the kill-and-return case. title: The dragon lair's 24 m edge has no hysteresis: after a give-up, a player pacing across it makes a new arrival at each crossing
evidence: frontend/src/world/bossSystem.js:99 (atLair: distance to the lair <= 24); PR #56 dynamic re-review (wf_04821fb2-3bc) finding A4, probe P1d
note: A design note, measured in jsdom: pacing between 23 m and 25 m every 2 s for 300 s gave 15 wakes, 16 give-ups, 48 failed loads, 32 danger flips and 1 entrance. It matches the design ('bounded by arrivals'), and the notice tells the player to leave the lair and come back. Fix if it shows in play: re-arm only past a wider radius than the wake's. Won't fix: follows DECISIONS 2026-10-30 item 121's arrival-bounded design (three retries per arrival, never on a timer); reaching the loop needs three failed chunk loads plus pacing the 24 m edge (15 wakes in 300 s, measured in jsdom).

title: Seven CodeQL alerts (five high, two medium) are open on main, all in repo scripts and tests; each needs a fix or a dismissal with its reason recorded
acceptance: `gh api repos/wowlegend/Crafty/code-scanning/alerts?state=open` returns no alert, or each remaining one is dismissed with its reason noted in this row.
evidence: GitHub code-scanning alerts 4-9 and 12, read 2026-10-31 via gh api; frontend/scripts/ci/bundle-budget.mjs:298 @a150a93a
note: CodeQL reports 'This does not escape backslash characters in the input.' at :276, the builder the W2-G census uses to find a hook name as a built chunk's quoted first argument. Read at :271-276: a name enters hookNames only through the literal match /^(['"`])([\w$]+)\1$/ at :272, which cannot contain a backslash, and the script reads this repo's own src, so no hostile input reaches the builder as written. It still stands as a high alert on main: 7 were open at the 2026-10-30 17:07-17:13Z read, 6 at Command Record v9, and this is the new one. Fix direction: escape every regex metacharacter in the name (name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')) or compare the chunk text as a string, then confirm the alert closes on the next scan; dismissing it as unreachable needs the reason recorded. The merged job sees a module nothing imports, which is what deleting a mount leaves, and no more. Fix: keep functionName for the functions that executed in the per-test coverage file, list MUST_REACH entries as module#symbol, and check the names against a real shard run first (V8 infers a name for `export const X = () =>` and `export function X`, not for a memo or forwardRef wrapper). Closed by lane L12 round 2 (DECISIONS item 350): MUST_REACH entries are module#function, the fixture keeps V8's functionName (tests/e2e/_coverage.js), the shard file /2 carries the named functions that ran, and the merge fails on an entry that ran in no shard, though its module was evaluated.

evidence: CI runs 41203933423 (5c568441) and 41208277637 (f0c027e6), shard 6/8: the spec ran out its budget, the e2e fixture read 'canvases unread (the page did not answer in 5 s)', and the runner was shut down minutes later, so no failure message survived; run 41206449396 (7019c838) passed it in 53.8 s. docs/superpowers/DECISIONS.md 2026-10-31 item 302. note: Seen as tests/e2e/music-bus.spec.js's page no longer answering on two of three CI runs when it entered from the title's Start Adventure. Round 1 held two hypotheses: (a) the entry, a trusted click on Start Adventure entering play outside _boot.js's startPlayActive, and (b) the music route through createMediaElementSource. Round 2 (DECISIONS 2026-10-31 item 306) refuted (b): with MusicPlayer making no track and no gesture callback the page stopped answering at least as often (off 10 of 15, on 5 of 16), once on the title before any click. While the page stalled, two Chromium processes grew to 15.6-15.8 GB of the runner's 16 GB in 6 of 12 jobs, and 5 runners were shut down, the end the two PR runs met. music-bus.spec.js now enters play the suite's way (the title entry passed 9 of 16 with the route on). title: The capture-guard ratchet does not follow a getter declared with `function` or a name that arrives through a re-export
acceptance: sourceFlow.js counts each call of a `function` getter and follows `export { x as y } from`, red first on the two probes in evidence as unit cases.
evidence: frontend/tests/_support/captureGuards.js (header: NOT FOLLOWED); frontend/tests/scripts/capture-guards-ratchet.test.js (header); frontend/tests/_support/sourceFlow.js. Measured at aa065c4a by calling captureGuards() on a two-file tree: an arrow getter held by a const with two uses counts 2, a `function frozen() { return isCaptureMode(); }` getter with the same two uses counts 1; an aliased import read twice counts 2, `export { isCaptureMode as frozen } from './devtest/captureMode.js'` with its importer reading `frozen()` twice counts 0. Round 2 dynamic review (mutants CG7 and CG8, both green on the real tree; controls CG7c arrow getter and the aliased import red). DECISIONS 2026-10-31 (lane L12, round 3) item 359.
note: Neither shape is in src today (the ledger is exact at 134 guards in 62 files), so no result is wrong now; src already re-exports in 18 lines, so the idiom is live. Round 2's DECISIONS item 351 and the two headers said a getter and any local name were followed; they are narrowed to what is proven (item 359). Fix: have sourceFlow.js bind a `function` declaration's returned read as a getter (its calls are the guards), and follow an `export { x as y } from` through its importers; red first with the two probes above as unit cases, mutation-proved. Or keep the narrowed claim and review for the two shapes. Opened by lane L12 round 3 (PR #71). A `function` getter counts once, not once per call; a re-exported name counts none; so a file can gain a guard through either with the ledger green.

title: Three MUST_REACH save-path entries are also run by specs that save themselves, so they read as ran if the game stopped saving
acceptance: MUST_REACH holds worldBoot.js#saveWorldInPlay, seen red on a throwaway ref with the game's own save call dropped; or runtime-reach.mjs keeps the group's claim narrowed.
evidence: frontend/scripts/ci/runtime-reach.mjs (MUST_REACH, the boot and save group; the note above it); frontend/tests/e2e/save-load.spec.js:28, forge.spec.js:250, quest-text.spec.js:163, talents.spec.js:380, the-cut.spec.js:150/300/434, load-hold.spec.js:84, continue.spec.js:150, world-rebuild-after-load.spec.js:83 (each `saveActiveWorld({ ... })` in the page, in the document the test ends on); frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx (saveActiveWorld calls buildSaveData and writeWorld); frontend/src/game/worldBoot.js (saveWorldInPlay, which App's autosave callback calls: src/App.jsx `save: () => saveWorldInPlay(...)`). Round 2 static review F1 and dynamic review N2 (derived, not run: no e2e).
note: V8 counts a call, not its caller. The mutant that drops the game's own save call (worldBoot.js's `st.saveActiveWorld(savePosition(st))` in saveWorldInPlay) is not seen by these three, and `installAutosave` still runs from App, so MUST_REACH would still read every entry as ran; other gates do see a save-path deletion (the static review names tests/gates/two-tab-save-gates.test.jsx and dead-refresh-gates.test.jsx; the dynamic review saw dead-refresh-gates and returning-player-gates red on a refused mutant). eventBus.js#emit is the one other entry a spec calls (context-loss.spec, before a reload). Fix: add `src/game/worldBoot.js#saveWorldInPlay` to the group if a spec's last document runs it through the autosave, and prove it red on a throwaway ref with the save call dropped (the ref is the command session's to push and delete); or narrow the group's claim, which the comment above MUST_REACH now does. Opened by lane L12 round 3 (PR #71). The three: saveActiveWorld, buildSaveData and writeWorld.

title: Nothing in the unit suite gates the e2e fixture's isolated-failure wiring: deleting its console listener or its throw stays green
acceptance: A unit test drives tests/e2e/_fixtures.js with a fake page and goes red on EI5 (the console listener deleted) and EI6 (the throw deleted).
evidence: frontend/tests/e2e/_fixtures.js:52 (`page.on('console', ...)`), :53 (the request listener) and :88 (`if (verdict.problem) throw`); frontend/tests/e2e/_isolatedFailures.js (the tracker, which tests/scripts/e2e-isolated-failures.test.js does cover); CI run 41229307736 (throwaway ref land/l12-fix2-mutants-2): smoke.spec failed all three attempts with '1 isolated failure(s) while this test ran (over 2 page load(s))'. note: Use is the only drink path (handleConsume, GamePanels.jsx:206-220), and every player starts with 2 Health and 1 Mana Potion. Fix trap: reusing stormBed's flat buffer makes the bed 33 dB louder RMS and 20 dB louder at peak, so it needs rescaling.

From the review tab's re-check (DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (ultrareview tab re-checks) item 469): confirmed with three's real shadow matrix: on the low tier the player's column leaves the map above y about 47 (terrain 39 to 63, spawn about 53); at y 53 the side away from the sun gets 20.5 of 56 m on medium and 50.5 of 72 m on high. Fix trap: snapShadowCentre snaps only x and z, so following the raw player y will probably shimmer shadow edges on a jump (not tested); capture pins the high tier, so the fix needs its own low-tier check.

title: Synth voices that sweep frequency use sin(2 pi f(t) t), twice the declared rate, so the fireball boom and hurl body turn around late in their decay

note: Partly reproduced: siegeHorn's step is 0.30x its own sawtooth edges (the finding's click claim is overstated). Not measured: slam, roar and aggroGrowl (closed form only). phase.js fixed three voices and does not claim the class closed. The sound by ear stays Kevin's.

title: SpatialAudioController and EnhancedMagicSystem read useState, context and subscribed values inside useFrame, against the Game-Loop Isolation rule

title: Night firefly drift is added once per frame with no delta, so fireflies move faster at higher frame rates and respawn four times as often at 120 fps

title: PROC_MUSIC_GAIN = 0 mutes the procedural music by gain only: the synth pad runs all session and, in a fight, the arpeggiator builds nodes into a zero gain
acceptance: With PROC_MUSIC_GAIN at 0 startSynthPad and startArpeggiator do not start and only the wind bed remains; a SoundProvider unit counts the started oscillators.
evidence: frontend/src/SoundManager.jsx:15, :134-242, :299-389 @dae1afb4; ultrareview 6-audio finding 9 (nit), our repro verifier: CONFIRMED in code and in a unit probe that drives the real SoundProvider; the cost was not measured in a browser; DECISIONS 2026-11-01 item 462

Battery and CPU on the iPad are unmeasured. From the review tab's re-check (DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (ultrareview tab re-checks) item 469): fix trap: startSynthPad also owns the wind bed and its 8 s step loop, so an early return for the muted music would kill the bed too; split the bed out first.

title: The Settings panel is about 1,100 px tall with no scroll, so Resume Game, Manage Worlds and Credits are off-screen at 1280x800, on iPad and on landscape phones
acceptance: At 1280x800, 1180x820 and 844x390 every Settings control, Resume Game included, is reachable (the card scrolls or fits); an e2e clicks Resume Game at each size.

The height is computed from classes: 13 rows in a gap-3 column, about 990-1,004 px of body plus a 74 px header and 35 px footer. Manage Worlds is the only way to load, save or switch a world, and Credits holds the CC BY attribution. Sibling panels already solve it (QuestLog max-h-[80vh], ControlsPanel overflow-y-auto, SpellUpgradePanel B5); e2e specs assert only toBeVisible, which Playwright satisfies off-screen. Building Tools (:558) and Inventory (:253) lose rows on landscape phones the same way. Lane: filed to W3-C as a first-minute reach, since Esc opens this panel and Resume Game is how a player leaves it; the plan's W3-C row names Unit 0, the hint strip, the title's Hearth and the first click after Start, not this, so the lane may hand it to backlog.

title: The joystick knob can stay pushed off-centre after the thumb lifts, because the release does not cancel the pending knob frame
acceptance: onEnd cancels the pending knob animation frame and only the move touch recentres the knob; a unit test with a fake rAF ends a touch before the frame and reads the knob centred.
evidence: frontend/src/ui/TouchControls.jsx:175-195 @dae1afb4; replica 4-ui votes C,C,C (LOW), one hunter; not re-verified by a probe; DECISIONS 2026-11-01 item 463

evidence: frontend/src/render/lookbookSeam.js:58 and :472, scripts/visual/_lookbook.mjs:466-467, scripts/visual/lookbook.mjs:468 @e5e1f745; W3-A PR A round 2: static review finding 1 (CONFIRMED in code) and dynamic review L1 (REPRODUCED with controls: a stray 1.0 m away and a ghost 0.2 m away both returned valid, 2.0 m and 3 m returned invalid)

Reachable only after a new cause of leftover models (the one known cause, useEntities, is fixed and gated, DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (W3-A PR A) item 430); the likeliest ghost sits under the next staged mob at the same 3.5 m spot. Harness LOW: it guards the combat frames W3-A's look claims rest on, so fix it when the lane next changes the combat set, or drop it.

title: force-place-mob-cell-gates leaves the own-column lift mutant alive; whether any gate catches a 2 m forced rise beside a wall-standing mob is unmeasured
acceptance: Under the mutant `sameColumn = false` either mob-wall-gates or mob-floor-gates goes red, or a new case (a forced block at a wall-standing mob's upper cell, a 2 m rise) does, red first.
evidence: frontend/src/game/localPath.js:225-226 (sameColumn lifts the mob), frontend/src/game/mobFloor.js:55-61 (the floor comes out 2 m up) and frontend/tests/gates/force-place-mob-cell-gates.test.jsx @84a04099; W3-A PR B round-2 static review, finding 3 (PLAUSIBLE, needs repro)
note: By reading, not run; the dynamic review did not run the repro. The gate fills only the mob's feet cell, a 1 m rise under STEP_UP 1.25 (localPath.js:39), so the step rule lifts the mob with or without the own-column exemption and the mutant survives. A block forced onto the wall face beside a mob standing against that wall, at its upper cell, gives faces [52, 51, 50] with feet at 50: the gap is not roomy, mobFloor's loop breaks and the floor is 52. Only the exemption lifts the mob then; without it the mob is rewound to its own spot every tick, embedded in the block. Repro, in a cp -c -R throwaway, from frontend/: npx vitest run tests/gates/mob-wall-gates.test.js --maxWorkers=2 and read the test count N, then sh scripts/dev/mutate.sh src/game/localPath.js tests/gates/mob-wall-gates.test.js N own-column-off 'const sameColumn = e.footX !== undefined && onOwnColumn(e);' 'const sameColumn = false;'; repeat both with tests/gates/mob-floor-gates.test.js. Whether C alone reaches the case depends on the aim cone, unresolved. DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (W3-A PR B) item 450.

title: On a Mac, hold C then press Cmd: a right-click should open the chest.
acceptance: Kevin holds C, presses Cmd, then right-clicks a chest on a real Mac keyboard: the chest opens and nothing is placed; he says so, or says what happened.
evidence: frontend/src/Components.jsx:471-472 (a keydown with Cmd or Ctrl down lets go of C) @84a04099; DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (W3-A PR B) item 449; W3-A PR B round-2 static review, 'Not checked': whether a real browser's MetaLeft or ControlLeft keydown carries its own modifier flag; the gate drives synthetic events and its docblock says this is cited, not measured
note: A real-device fact; no agent can confirm a Mac keyboard. Item 449 lets go of C on any keydown with Cmd or Ctrl down because macOS sends no keyup for a key let go while Cmd is down (Mozilla bug 1299553), and force-place-key-gates proves the release with synthetic key events only. If the real keydown does not carry the flag, C stays held after Cmd and every right click at a chest or a mob places. Ctrl on Windows and Linux is the same check. Nothing is blocked on it.

title: A placed block's place sound may be muffled to 350 Hz by the new cell's own collider, which the occlusion march counts as up to 5 walls (disputed)
acceptance: A probe in the real GameScene mount order places a block and reads the lowpass its place voice gets: muffled means the march starts outside the emitter's cell, never reached means close it false-positive with the probe.
evidence: frontend/src/render/SpatialAudioController.jsx:31-75 @267110a4 (unchanged since dae1afb4); ultrareview 6-audio-scene-rest finding 6 (nit); our repro verifier: REFUTED on reachability (DECISIONS 2026-11-01 item 462); the review tab's re-check: NARROWED, not refuted, with a real-Rapier model of 20,000 placements (docs/superpowers/audits/2026-11-01-ultrareview/6-audio-scene-rest.tab-recheck.md); DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (ultrareview tab re-checks) item 469
note: Two verdicts, severity LOW until a tie-break. Ours (item 462): every line-level claim is true, but the block-place sound never reaches the spatial path in GameScene's mount order, so nothing is heard; no row was filed then. The tab's (item 469): the real Rapier engine and the same march give 5 walls in 31% of 20,000 modelled top-face placements, 3 or more hits (350 Hz) in 55% and none in 16%, and the voice lasts only 0.1 s. They measure different things: ours asks whether the sound reaches the march at all, the tab's how muffled it is when it does, and the tab's summary reports no reachability check, so both may hold. The tab's figures come from a model of placements, not from the game. Filed here so the dispute has a row; the probe in the acceptance settles it.

title: The wind bed's gain ramps toward the volume the pad started with, so a later volume change never reaches the bed while the pad plays
acceptance: The wind bed's step ramp reads the current volume (a ref or the store), not the render-time closure; a fake-AudioParam test changes volume mid-pad and sees the next ramp target use it.
evidence: frontend/src/SoundManager.jsx:235 with the volume effect at :259-266 @267110a4 (unchanged since dae1afb4); found by the 6-audio-scene-rest review tab's re-check, not in the cloud's 10 (docs/superpowers/audits/2026-11-01-ultrareview/6-audio-scene-rest.tab-recheck.md); not yet independently reproduced by a probe; DECISIONS 2026-11-01 (ultrareview tab re-checks) item 469
note: Read at 267110a4 for this row: the 8 s step callback closes over the volume of the render that started the pad, and the volume effect updates only the pad's masterGain. No shipped UI calls setVolume (its only caller is tests/gates/event-sound-gates.test.jsx:112), so volume stays 0.5 and nothing is audible today: filed as LOW debt by item 462's rule for harm NONE; it becomes a bug the day a volume control is wired. The same step loop holds AUDIT:ultra-1101:6-audio-scene-rest-2's ramps, whose anchor fix touches this line. The plan gives LANE:W2-M the sample bank and the night's voices, not the beds, so it sits in backlog with the other bed rows.
